text:
Ryan Nugent-Hopkins took a puck to the face against Vancouver on November 7 and left after 6.6 minutes. He was back two nights later, wearing a bubble, per the Edmonton Journal, and the Oilers have won all four games since. He hasn't scored in any of them: four straight without a point, on 2.7 expected points, and his chances have thinned too.

The season line is still strong for a 33-year-old still with the team that drafted him first overall in 2011: 11 points in 12 games, 3.02 points per hour against his 2.45 last season. Lean on the power play to explain it. Seven of his 11 points have come with the man advantage, and his teammates have been scoring 4.61 more goals than expected with him on.

At five on five, Edmonton has had 46.75% of the expected goals with him out there, roughly what it gets without him. Watch the even-strength chances over the next couple of weeks. If they stay this thin, the power play will have to carry him.
headline: Nugent-Hopkins, back in a bubble
